title: "Re-register after merger" via link and PIN vs. merger notice with account unchanged
summary: A caller from Narmada Cooperative Bank tells the recipient that the bank is merging with Kaveri Bank. In the fraud case, the caller says every account must be "re-registered" today or it will be frozen, sends a link, and asks the recipient to enter their account number, debit card details, and ATM PIN there. In the legitimate case, the caller announces the merger date and says the account continues automatically, with the same passbook, cheque book, and card. Nothing needs to be done, and any later changes will be announced at the branch and by letter.

shared_setting.pretext: the merger takes effect on a date two to four weeks away.
shared_setting.recipient_profile: an adult long-time cooperative-bank member, often in a smaller town; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Both callers say "after the merger" and mention that customers will "become Kaveri Bank customers". Balance of about [AMOUNT_1] (₹10,000–₹5,00,000) may be mentioned.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller directs the recipient to an unofficial link and asks them to enter card details and ATM PIN, under a threat of freezing. A merger transfers accounts automatically and never needs customers' secret credentials.
fraud.caller_objective: Capture the recipient's account number, card number, and ATM PIN on a look-alike page.
stable_facts: Link: https://narmada-kaveri-merger.invalid/register (sent by SMS during the call).
Deadline: "today", or the account will be frozen "until you visit the head office".
The page shows both banks' names and asks for account number, card number, expiry, and ATM PIN.

legitimate.label_rationale: The caller informs the recipient of a merger and says nothing is needed from them. No link, credential, or payment is asked.
legitimate.caller_objective: Reassure the recipient that the account continues and tell them where to get information.
stable_facts: From the merger date, Narmada branches work as Kaveri Bank branches. The recipient's account continues with its balance, and the account number, passbook, cheque book, and card keep working until further notice (fictional arrangement for this card).
Any later change, such as a new card or app, will be announced by letter and on the branch notice board, with time to act.
The caller says the bank will never ask for a PIN, password, or OTP because of the merger.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may insist on the link, resend it, or increase urgency. They must not switch to a different mechanism (for example payment or an app install). The legitimate caller must not send a link or ask for credentials after the branch.

must_preserve: both bank names and the merger in both
link plus card and ATM PIN request with same-day freeze (_F)
automatic continuation, no registration, and explicit "no PIN/password" (_L)
may_vary: up to 2 filler turns before turn 3

ambiguities: Merger", "update", and "Kaveri Bank" appear in both cases. The label depends on the link and credential request.

In real mergers, account numbers or IFSC codes may change later, with notice. This card fixes them as unchanged for the notice period as a fictional arrangement. Generators must not state a real rule.
The legitimate caller's mention of a future new card or app is a deliberate confound. It must stay in the future, announced by letter and at the branch, with no link.
Mechanism overlap: the same as bp_02 (link plus credentials under a freeze threat), with a merger pretext and a cooperative-bank recipient.

evidence_references.claim: In an RBI-sanctioned amalgamation, the transferee opens corresponding accounts with full balances; branches function as its branches (CB30)
Banks never ask for PIN, password, or OTP (C01)
Calls threatening account blocking with a link to "update" are a common fraud (C04)
Fraud can be reported on 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in (C12)
